units.text: Begin with the two client VPCs on the left, whose associations connect their clients to the central VPC Lattice service network.
Follow the orders and payments services across the middle: each uses a listener, routing rules, and a target group to reach its application targets.
The lower panels connect service DNS, optional IAM authorization policies, and observability, which together support controlled application requests across VPCs and accounts.
With the complete architecture visible, distinguish managed service access through Lattice from general network routing through Transit Gateway or publishing an endpoint service through PrivateLink.
Start at the authorization gate: requests requiring an authenticated identity are signed, while anonymous access depends on the configured authorization mode and policies.
Follow the listener rules in the middle, which are evaluated by priority, with the default action used when no earlier rule matches.
Continue to the target group and the observation path below, checking target health and using access logs and metrics to investigate errors and latency.
Returning to the whole path, check both service network and service authorization where enabled, because an explicit deny blocks the request even when routing is correct.
